newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Dutch premier confident of deal on EU reform.
newsitem.headline: Dutch premier confident of deal on EU reform.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, racing against time to secure a deal on European Union reform, said on Monday that he was confident accord could be reached by next month's Amsterdam summit.
"The political will exists all over Europe to bring this...to a successful end," he told a news conference in Lisbon.
Kok, whose country holds the EU presidency, is on a three-country tour to push plans to revise the workings of the 15-nation bloc to prepare it for the entry of new members.
After meeting Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, Kok left for Spain for talks there. He was due to visit Italy on Tuesday.
He said his discussions in Lisbon had been "encouraging."
"Portugal is a strong and convinced partner in the process of European cooperation," he said.
